prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Added the tasklist extension with configurable checkboxes and item classes. All 1,133 tests passed, with 110 skipped.

+---
+title: Task Lists
+---
+
+# Task Lists
+
+The Task Lists extension converts list items beginning with `[ ]`, `[x]`, or
+`[X]` followed by a space into checkbox items. It supports ordered, unordered,
+nested, and loose lists. Inline Markdown after the marker is still processed.
+
+```python
+markdown.markdown(text, extensions=['tasklist'])
+```
+
+By default, checkboxes are disabled and task items have the `task` class.
+Configure the extension to make checkboxes clickable or change the class:
+
+```python
+markdown.markdown(text, extensions=['tasklist'], extension_configs={
+    'tasklist': {'clickable': True, 'item_class': 'todo'}
+})
+```
+
+Set `item_class` to an empty string to omit the added class. Clickable
+checkboxes only change their state in the browser; the extension does not
+persist that state.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/markdown/extensions/tasklist.py
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+"""Convert list item markers into disabled or clickable checkboxes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from xml.etree import ElementTree as etree
+
+from . import Extension
+from ..treeprocessors import Treeprocessor
+
+
+TASK_RE = re.compile(r'^\[([ xX])\] ')
+
+
+class TaskListTreeprocessor(Treeprocessor):
+    """Replace task markers before inline processing."""
+
+    def __init__(self, md, clickable, item_class):
+        super().__init__(md)
+        self.clickable = clickable
+        self.item_class = item_class
+
+    def run(self, root):
+        for item in root.iter('li'):
+            container = item
+            if not item.text and len(item) and item[0].tag == 'p':
+                container = item[0]
+            match = TASK_RE.match(container.text or '')
+            if match is None:
+                continue
+            checkbox = etree.Element('input', {'type': 'checkbox'})
+            if match.group(1) != ' ':
+                checkbox.set('checked', 'checked')
+            if not self.clickable:
+                checkbox.set('disabled', 'disabled')
+            checkbox.tail = ' ' + container.text[match.end():]
+            container.text = None
+            container.insert(0, checkbox)
+            if self.item_class:
+                item.set('class', ' '.join(filter(None, (item.get('class'), self.item_class))))
+
+
+class TaskListExtension(Extension):
+    """Add checkboxes to list items beginning with task markers."""
+
+    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
+        self.config = {
+            'clickable': [False, 'Allow checkboxes to be clicked.'],
+            'item_class': ['task', 'Class added to task list items.'],
+        }
+        super().__init__(**kwargs)
+
+    def extendMarkdown(self, md):
+        md.treeprocessors.register(
+            TaskListTreeprocessor(md, self.getConfig('clickable'), self.getConfig('item_class')),
+            'tasklist', 25
+        )
+
+
+def makeExtension(**kwargs):  # pragma: no cover
+    return TaskListExtension(**kwargs)

+"""Tests for the task list extension."""
+
+import unittest
+import xml.etree.ElementTree as etree
+
+import markdown
+
+
+class TestTaskList(unittest.TestCase):
+    def convert(self, source, **config):
+        html = markdown.markdown(
+            source, extensions=['tasklist'], extension_configs={'tasklist': config}
+        )
+        return etree.fromstring('<root>' + html + '</root>')
+
+    def test_markers_and_inline_markup(self):
+        root = self.convert('- [ ] *open*\n- [x] **done**\n- [X] [link](https://example.com)')
+        items = root.findall('./ul/li')
+        self.assertEqual(len(items), 3)
+        for item in items:
+            self.assertEqual(item.get('class'), 'task')
+            self.assertEqual(item[0].attrib.get('type'), 'checkbox')
+            self.assertEqual(item[0].attrib.get('disabled'), 'disabled')
+        self.assertNotIn('checked', items[0][0].attrib)
+        self.assertTrue(all(item[0].get('checked') == 'checked' for item in items[1:]))
+        self.assertEqual([item[1].tag for item in items], ['em', 'strong', 'a'])
+
+    def test_ordered_nested_and_loose_lists(self):
+        root = self.convert('1. [ ] parent\n\n    - [X] nested\n\n2. [x] second\n\n   More text.')
+        items = root.findall('.//li')
+        self.assertEqual(len(items), 3)
+        for item in items:
+            self.assertEqual(item.get('class'), 'task')
+            self.assertIsNotNone(item.find('.//input'))
+        self.assertEqual(items[0].find('./p/input').get('type'), 'checkbox')
+        self.assertEqual(items[1].find('./input').get('checked'), 'checked')
+        self.assertEqual(items[2].find('./p/input').get('checked'), 'checked')
+
+    def test_configuration(self):
+        root = self.convert('- [x] done', clickable=True, item_class='todo')
+        item = root.find('./ul/li')
+        self.assertEqual(item.get('class'), 'todo')
+        self.assertNotIn('disabled', item[0].attrib)
+        root = self.convert('- [ ] task', item_class='')
+        self.assertNotIn('class', root.find('./ul/li').attrib)
+
+    def test_nonmarkers(self):
+        root = self.convert('- [ ]\n- [x]no space\n- [y] other\n- prefix [x] task\n\n[x] paragraph')
+        self.assertEqual(len(root.findall('.//input')), 0)
+        self.assertTrue(all('class' not in item.attrib for item in root.findall('./ul/li')))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()
